title: How the web works
goal: Follow a page request from your browser to a server.
explanation: A browser requests resources from a server. A URL identifies a resource; DNS helps resolve a hostname to an IP address. HTTPS protects the connection with TLS.
The server sends a response with a status, headers and a body. HTML describes the page, CSS controls presentation, and JavaScript adds behaviour. They may arrive in separate responses.
Open browser developer tools and the Network tab, reload a page, and inspect the document request. A 404 means the requested resource was not found; it does not mean your computer is broken.
code:
GET /about HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html
exercise: Inspect one document request. Record its method, status and Content-Type.
hint: Look for the request with type document in the Network tab.

quiz.question: Which resource usually defines the structure of a web page?
quiz.explanation: HTML describes the content and structure. CSS controls its presentation.
